overview.title: History holds records; Selection defines their meaning
overview.explanation: The History-to-Snapshot edge means owned value storage. History-to-Selection is a borrowed dependency. Selection can read Snapshot internals because of friendship, a C++ access rule; the creation/read arrow is a teaching dependency and does not mean Selection owns every saved snapshot.

focus.title: Copy the interval into and out of a record
focus.what: These operations define exactly which state a snapshot captures.
focus.where: Selection owns both operations because it knows its private representation.
focus.why: Outside history code can keep a value without accessing either endpoint.
focus.invariant: Both endpoints are copied, and saved values remain unchanged.
focus.risk: Reference-based snapshots would track live changes instead of preserving history.

focus.title: Restore first, consume history second
focus.what: This operation restores the newest saved state if one exists.
focus.where: History supplies ordering but cannot inspect snapshot fields.
focus.why: The recovery record should remain available until restoration succeeds.
focus.invariant: An empty history returns false and changes no selection state.
focus.risk: Popping before a potentially throwing restore would lose the only record needed to retry.
